correctness.rationale: In the centered two-dimensional plane, P-Pi is nonzero rank-one nilpotent and equals sigma uv^T with orthonormal u,v. The reversed mixture squares to sigma^2 p(1-p)(I-Pi), which proves all exact correlation/power/eigenvalue statements including endpoints. Trigonometric cyclic products and positivity give sigma<=sqrt(3)-1. The radical matrix has row and column sums 1, nonnegative entries, square Pi, and sigma=sqrt(3)-1, yielding equality. Two-state impossibility follows from centered dimension one. Branch lengths R_ij/3 and slopes 1/R_ij prove the explicit interval realization. A 345-assertion exact checker corroborates examples and powers; universality rests on proof.

originality.rationale: Published general annealed spectral formulas and generic convex-mixture slowdown are prior knowledge, not asserted as novel. The checked statements do not give the three-state optimal singular-value and resonance threshold sqrt(3)-1 with finite-time exact deterministic mixing, nor the universal even-lag identity and sharp expanding-map realization. value.rationale: This is an exact classification and sharp optimal spectral strength for a natural minimal-dimensional time-reversal mixing paradox, rather than an isolated numeric Markov example. Fixed constituents reach exact equilibrium in two steps but their random combination has positive correlations at every even lag. The exact sqrt(3)-1 bound and extremizer give a quantitative impossibility/attainability boundary for observable-sector annealed resonances, with a genuine expanding one-dimensional dynamical realization. It motivates studying optimal randomization-induced memory in more complex Markov models.
